svg.title: Four Gates Before a Division Order Gets Signed
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-division-order-gates; chapter number: 5; title: Four Gates Before a Division Order Gets Signed; subtitle: Rebuild the decimal, strike the extras, return the W-9, watch operator changes; chart type: decision_tree; nodes: gate: G1; question: Does your rebuilt decimal (NMA divided by unit acres times royalty) match the order?; pass next: G2; fail action: Call the division order department, tell them they made a mistake or to convince you otherwise, and ask for the redacted title opinion pages covering your interest.; gate: G2; question: Is the order free of extra clauses, operator-liability terms and cost-deduction language?; pass next: G3; fail action: On a Texas order, strike and initial every clause beyond the statutory list and return with proof of delivery, or substitute the NADOA model form.; gate: G3; question: Is a W-9 on file with the paying company?; pass next: G4; fail action: Return the W-9 no matter what, even on Oklahoma wells you refuse to sign, to avoid roughly 28% backup withholding.; gate: G4; question: Does the decimal hold when a new operator sends its own order?; pass next: Sign, then keep checking each stub against the lease fraction; fail action: Treat the change as a red flag and make the new operator show how it built the number.; caption: Matt Sands' benchmark is 160/1,280 times 18.75%, or 0.0234375. Mineral View shows that a half-size decimal on a $100,000-a-month well costs $187,500 over 20 years.; assumptions note: Blue Mesa Minerals reports problems with maybe 2 of about 130 operators on the NADOA form. Richard Winblad advises never signing even that form in Oklahoma, citing 12% interest compounded annually on late pay.; note: Attributed to NARO (W3POOsq6ka0), Matt Sands (tJr4jiz31fw), Royalty Clerk (DN-VIoSmyF0, blbomhUd0sA), Blue Mesa Minerals (SfX6ycoYg24), Richard Winblad (iD4uCjptCXM) and Mineral View (KYu7M4t5LAk) on YouTube.

text.title: Four Gates Before a Division Order Gets Signed
text.tspan: Four Gates Before a Division Order Gets Signed

rect.title: gate: G1; question: Does your rebuilt decimal (NMA divided by unit acres times royalty) match the order?; pass next: G2; fail action: Call the division order department, tell them they made a mistake or to convince you otherwise, and ask for the redacted title opinion pages covering your interest.

gate: G2; question: Is the order free of extra clauses, operator-liability terms and cost-deduction language?; pass next: G3; fail action: On a Texas order, strike and initial every clause beyond the statutory list and return with proof of delivery, or substitute the NADOA model form.

gate: G3; question: Is a W-9 on file with the paying company?; pass next: G4; fail action: Return the W-9 no matter what, even on Oklahoma wells you refuse to sign, to avoid roughly 28% backup withholding.

gate: G4; question: Does the decimal hold when a new operator sends its own order?; pass next: Sign, then keep checking each stub against the lease fraction; fail action: Treat the change as a red flag and make the new operator show how it built the number.

text.title: Assumptions: Blue Mesa Minerals reports problems with maybe 2 of about 130 operators on the NADOA form. Richard Winblad advises never signing even that form in Oklahoma, citing 12% interest compounded annually on late pay.
